clue.text: Sensitive insular person talked oddly

parts.note: a Brit is a native of the British Isles, an island dweller

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions of the word talked

explanation.surface: Someone touchy from an island spoke in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'talked', giving TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensitive in the sense of fragile or easily broken can be described with this adjective.

clue.text: Exchange part of meal, getting better standard of starter

indicators.note: the first letter, a C grade, is raised to the better grade of B

parts.note: a course is one stage of a meal

explanation.surface: A dinner course upgraded with a finer starter.
explanation.walkthrough: Grades run A, B, C, so a B is a better standard than a C: the C opening the word becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bourse is a stock exchange, especially the Paris one, where shares are traded.

clue.text: Take in one graduate after setting up IT firm

indicators.note: after says the graduate comes behind the reversed firm

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: setting up, in a down clue, says the firm's letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: IBM is a computing company
BE is a Bachelor of Engineering

explanation.surface: A graduate joins after an IT company is set up and absorbs them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reads upwards in a down clue, a reversal; 'after' places the graduate last. BE is Bachelor of Engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink or absorb, so it means take in, as of liquid or ideas.

clue.text: Solid earth company put in ground at rear

indicators.note: put in says the company goes inside the reworked letters
ground means crushed, so the letters of at rear are broken up and reformed

parts.note: a firm is a company

explanation.surface: A company placed on land behind the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns AT REAR into TERRAA, and 'put in' places FIRM within: TERRA-FIRM-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for firm land, dry land as opposed to sea or air.

clue.text: Woman taking out books of amorous literature

indicators.note: taking out says the books are removed from the literature

parts.note: erotica is sexually explicit writing
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A woman removing racy novels from the shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Supports forming most of base in ship

indicators.note: in says the trimmed base goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the word for base is dropped

parts.note: a plinth is the base a statue stands on

explanation.surface: Props made largely from the foundations of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a naval base but is a statue's plinth; 'most of' drops its last letter and 'in' puts what remains inside the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Splints are rigid strips strapped to a broken limb to hold it steady, so they are supports.

clue.text: Good person with space in a shelter for relation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: in says the space goes inside a shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A saint who needs room in a tent for a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a printer's space, a convention worth knowing; 'in' sets it within the shelter. 'relation' means an account, not a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation can be an account or report, as in the relating of events, which a statement is.

clue.text: Woman having cause to lie about daughter

indicators.note: about says the verb surrounds the daughter's letter

parts.note: to lay something down is to make it lie

explanation.surface: A mother with reason to lie on her daughter's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cause to lie' looks like a motive for lying, but it means the verb lay; 'about' wraps it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite word for a woman.

clue.text: Doing 6 billion plus 4

parts.note: the answer at 6 down is a titled woman, and a nob is a person of high social rank
the answer at 4 down is the heather genus, and ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A sum of six billion and four, read as arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to other answers: 6 down is a titled woman, an example of a nob; 4 down is heather, of which ling is a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing someone, in British slang, is cheating or conning them, as is nobbling, which also means tampering.

clue.text: Anagram set daily in consistent manner

indicators.note: the clue simply names the device, asking for the letters of set daily rearranged

explanation.surface: Set daily anagrams, done reliably every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something steadily means doing it evenly, without faltering, in a regular way.

clue.text: Brownish-coloured river in the East End

indicators.note: East End cockney speech famously drops the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary river in northern England

explanation.surface: A river of a dull brown shade found in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is a river in north-east England; a cockney from London's East End drops the opening H.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earthy pigment, so as an adjective it names a dark brownish colour.

clue.text: Car manufacturer, British, invested in new line that's silent

indicators.note: invested in says the car maker and British go inside the reworked word
new says the letters of line are made afresh in another order

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

explanation.surface: A German car firm putting money into a fresh product range that runs noiselessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges line to INLE, and 'invested in' is a containment signal, not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be heard at all makes no sound, which is what silent describes.

clue.text: Deputy grabbed by Tuareg, an ambush backfired

indicators.note: backfired says the hidden letters are read backwards
grabbed by says the answer is held within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sheriff's deputy is seized in a desert ambush by Tuareg nomads that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Deputy grabbed' as the definition, but 'grabbed by' is the hiding signal and 'Deputy' alone defines. 'backfired' reads REGANAMBUS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A submanager ranks just below the manager and stands in for them, which is a deputy's role.

clue.text: Large dons mock idiot

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the mock word wears the large letter inside it

parts.note: cod, as an adjective, means sham or mock

explanation.surface: Many university dons ridicule a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb, putting on: COD wraps L.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a dull, stupid person, a blockhead, which is the sense of idiot here.

clue.text: Seeing Pennywise the clown with head in arm

indicators.note: in says the clown and the headland go inside the arm

parts.note: a wing is an arm of a building or organisation
Pennywise is the clown monster in Stephen King's novel It
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A sighting of a horror clown, arm in arm with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Pennywise is the monster in Stephen King's novel It; a ness is a headland, hence 'head'. 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Witnessing an event means observing it with your own eyes, so it is seeing.

clue.text: Unrestricted record of organ tissue hiding nothing

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: hiding says the word for nothing is concealed inside the adjective

parts.note: retinal means relating to the retina, the light-sensitive tissue of the eye
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An open-ended recording of an organ's tissue with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' is the eye, whose tissue is the retina; 'hiding' puts nothing, the round letter, inside, giving RETIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A discretional choice is left to one's own judgment, so it is not bound by rules: free, unrestricted.

clue.text: Rectorship being cut short devastated churchgoer

indicators.note: devastated says the remaining letters are ruined and reassembled
being cut short says the final letter of Rectorship is lopped off

explanation.surface: A curtailed term as rector left a parishioner distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut short' drops the P of RECTORSHIP, and 'devastated' rearranges RECTORSHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister sings in a church choir, so is one who goes to church regularly.

clue.text: Nymph gains heart of old man, one's struck

indicators.note: gains says the nymph takes the other letters inside her

parts.note: a naiad is a water nymph

indicators.note: heart of asks for the central letter of the word old

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A nymph wins an old man's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' picks the middle letter of old, and 'gains' is the containment signal; 'one's struck' means the thing a hammer hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A nailhead is the flat top of a nail, the part hit by the hammer.

clue.text: Switching between Italy and Spain, type of weather's changed for plant

indicators.note: Italy and Spain have the international vehicle codes I and E, which trade places in the weather word
changed confirms the weather word is altered by the swap

parts.note: the climate is the typical weather of a region, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A plant whose climate changes as it moves between Italy and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: I is Italy's and E is Spain's car code; swapping them in CLIMATES turns CL-I-MAT-E-S into CL-E-MAT-I-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing garden plant with large showy flowers.

clue.text: A grind being retired worker — consuming alcohol is crucial

indicators.note: consuming says the reversed grinding word and the insect swallow the wine between them
being retired means withdrawn, so the grinding word goes back to front

parts.note: to mill is to grind, as grain
the ant is the crossword's favourite worker
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A retired worker, once in a dreary grind, now drinks heavily, which is vital to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reads as a pensioner but is the reversal signal (giving LLIM), and 'consuming' is a containment that spans the reversed word and the insect together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-important matters above everything else, so it is vital or crucial.

clue.text: Bad function not totally packed

parts.note: sin, the sine, is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: not totally says the last letter is missing from the packed word

parts.note: full means packed

explanation.surface: A faulty function that isn't completely filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN is the sine function in maths; 'not totally' cuts FULL to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful conduct is wicked or morally wrong, which is what bad means here.

clue.text: Kept raising points about school subject

indicators.note: about says the reversed points wrap around the subject
raising, in a down clue, says the word for points reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: dots are small points
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Raising points about a subject taught at school, kept on file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' in a down clue reads upwards, giving STOD; 'about' is the containment. RE is religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stored has been put away and kept for later use.

clue.text: Pest eating this cake would get most fat

definitions.text: Pest eating this cake would get most fat

parts.words: Pest eating this cake would get most fat
parts.note: the word for a cake of soap, set inside the letters of Pest, makes the superlative meaning fattest; the cake sense also defines it

explanation.surface: A greedy pest that ate this cake would end up the fattest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the answer: set inside P-EST it builds the superlative of plump.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake of soap or a solid mass of something is a compact chunk, which the answer also names.

clue.text: Morris dancing with stick, start to remove clothing

indicators.note: dancing says the letters jig about into a new order
start to remove says the first letter of stick is taken away

explanation.surface: Morris dancers, sticks in hand, begin stripping off their costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is an English folk dance done with sticks. 'start to remove' cuts STICK to TICK; 'dancing' rearranges MORRIS and TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A microskirt is an extremely short skirt, so it is a garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Fling with this equestrian, perhaps, makes girlfriend mad

indicators.note: mad says the letters of girlfriend are scrambled, made from the fling's letters plus the answer's

explanation.surface: A dalliance with a horseman drives one's partner wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the answer: FLING plus it, shuffled ('mad'), gives GIRLFRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is one who rides horses, an example of someone on horseback, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Vessel going over a swimmer

indicators.note: going over, in a down clue, says the vessel sits above the next letter

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A boat passing over a swimmer in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is TUN, a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean fish, so it is a swimmer, a cryptic way of naming a fish.

clue.text: Gave responsibility to hospital department past its prime

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
rusted means corroded with age, no longer at its best

explanation.surface: Someone handed a run-down hospital unit to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust someone is to hand them a duty or trust, so it means put them in charge of something.

clue.text: Kind endlessly backing official reason

indicators.note: endlessly says the word Kind loses both its first and last letters
backing says the official's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is a match official

explanation.surface: A kind sort, without end, supporting an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves IN from KIND; 'backing' turns REF into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or work something out by logic, which is to reason as a verb.

clue.text: Some French couple lose heart

parts.note: des is French for some
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A few French couples become disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all hope, to become discouraged, which is losing heart.

clue.text: Feasted with relation to King Edward

parts.note: regal means relating to or fit for a king
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A banquet held in honour of King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to entertain them lavishly with food and drink, so it means feasted, as a transitive verb.
